name: Cold desert
notes: Sparse grey chenopod shrubs (saltbush, saxaul, winterfat) and scattered bunchgrasses with cold winters; Gobi and Central Asian deserts, Great Basin/Colorado Plateau lowlands, Patagonian monte.

shrub.name: Saltbush
shrub.source: Atriplex canescens (fourwing saltbush), western N American deserts, grey shrub 0.5-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Saxaul
shrub.source: Haloxylon ammodendron, Gobi and Central Asian sand/gravel deserts, leafless twisted shrub-tree 2-8 m — Flora of China

shrub.name: Winterfat
shrub.source: Krascheninnikovia ceratoides, Eurasian and N American cold deserts, woolly grey sub-shrub 0.3-1 m — Flora of China / USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Blackbrush
shrub.source: Coleogyne ramosissima, Mojave-Great Basin transition, dark twiggy shrub 0.3-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Mormon tea
shrub.source: Ephedra nevadensis, Great Basin and Mojave, leafless jointed green shrub 0.5-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Reaumuria
shrub.source: Reaumuria soongarica, dominant dwarf shrub of Gobi gravel deserts, 20-60 cm — Flora of China

ground.name: Indian ricegrass
ground.source: Achnatherum hymenoides, sandy cold deserts of western N America, 30-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Galleta grass
ground.source: Pleuraphis jamesii, Colorado Plateau and Great Basin desert grass, 20-50 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Gobi needlegrass
ground.source: Stipa glareosa, gravel deserts of Mongolia and Xinjiang, small tussock 10-30 cm — Flora of China

ground.name: Desert halogeton
ground.source: Anabasis brevifolia, Gobi and Kazakh stony deserts, succulent dwarf cushion 5-25 cm — Flora of China

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.
